Only the artifact's own G1 disclosure surfaced the gate violation — the evaluator's check methodology could not detect it.

HOWEVER, the node's intended role in the graph is the 'last gate' that 'runs only after review-product-coherence corrects the product' (node why + constraint), so it 'never audits a product the reviewer just flagged.' This completion audits a product that was never reviewed or corrected: review-product-coherence is provisional with reviews/product-coherence.md absent, milestone-integration is provisional with its criteria unevidenced, and the mirror advanced the frontier to this terminal node anyway. Prior lane-2 attempts (1-3) already blocked on this same unmet dependency gate; the gate is still unmet — only the artifact has changed. Completing the terminal gate in this state lets the graph record a final-gate completion whose precondition never held, risking a false graph closure/release with every upstream node still provisional and the walkthrough outcome the graph promises never achieved. That is a subtle veer from the node's role-as-stated (drift) rather than active harm (the work documents the problem impeccably and defers the release decision to the human), so this is not a block — but a human MUST look before this node is treated as the graph's finished release gate: either complete milestone-integration and review-product-coherence and re-run the audit, or formally accept this audit as a non-compliant baseline.
